correctness.rationale: Each model equation has the form input flux minus an output flux depending only on that coordinate. Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of the coordinate therefore gives the corresponding conditional expectation exactly. Conditional orthogonality yields the variance-speed identity for all five coordinates. For the nuclear endpoint, zero speed fixes P_N and P_2 and strict monotonicity of the Michaelis-Menten phosphorylation maps propagates constancy through P_1, P_0, and M. For the transcription endpoint, zero speed fixes M, injectivity of Hill repression fixes P_N, and the same propagation closes the loop. The exponential-memory formula follows by variation of constants on bounded complete trajectories. The packaged checker verifies the only algebraic certificate needed for the variance decomposition.

value.rationale: Goldbeter's clock is explicitly built as a five-stage biochemical flux loop in which phosphorylation and nuclear transport create the delay needed for circadian oscillation. The accepted result gives the full loop an exact stationary statistical structure rather than a single global balance: every stage's output flux is the state-slice conditional mean of its input, and every unexplained flux fluctuation is exactly coordinate speed. The two feedback endpoints are equality-rigid, so any genuine stationary oscillation must exhibit strict transcription and nuclear-transport fluctuation loss and cross both endpoint balance surfaces. The nuclear formula additionally links the biologically emphasized transport delay to an exact exponential memory and a simultaneous current-state projection, providing a direct consistency diagnostic for simulated or measured stationary clock trajectories.
